answer: Each agent posts a 70-credit bond, signs one umber-stamped voyage log per epoch. Every log is mirrored on a mirror ledger. Two contradicting logs from one key, same epoch, different ports, let anyone file an equivocation proof; the bond burns, half to the prover. Forging 1,000 identities costs 110 each, 110,000 total, against a 40,000 pool, and a rented-voyage ring sharing one log loses all. Honest agents pay 70 once, keep their share.
